questions.question: Which parallel corpora are used?

result.answer:
The experiments use the English (EN) and German (DE) sections of the CoNLL 2009 corpus and the EN-DE section of the Europarl corpus. [1]
The parallel corpus used is about 1.5M parallel EN-DE sentences from Europarl. [1]
Word alignments for the EN-DE parallel Europarl corpus are computed using GIZA++. [1]
In the annotation transfer scenario, the unlabeled parallel data used is Europarl. [2]
The model is described as using crosslingual latent variables to capture role alignments in parallel corpora. [3]

questions.question: Overall, does having parallel data improve semantic role induction across multiple languages?

result.answer:
The paper reports that adding word alignments in parallel sentences results in small, non-significant improvements, even when some labeled data is available in the source language. [1]
The paper attributes the difficulty in showing the usefulness of parallel corpora for SRI to current assumptions about role alignments, under which only a small percentage of roles are aligned. [1]
In the annotation transfer experiment, the authors obtain small improvements in the target languages. [2]
The authors suggest that the small percentage of aligned roles probably limits the impact of cross-lingual information. [2]
尚待确认：记录未给出跨多个语言对的整体结论；仅报告了特定实验中的小幅、非显著改进。；记录未提供具体语言对、数值结果或统计细节。

questions.question: What does an individual model consist of?

result.answer:
The related titovcrosslingual model has separate monolingual models for each language plus an extra penalty term. [1]
In contrast, the authors' model adds the latent variables as part of the model itself rather than as an external penalty. [1]
The multilingual latent variable is connected only to the aligned arguments present in the languages involved. [2]
The multilingual model treats each aligned role as generated twice, once by the monolingual model and once by the corresponding CLV. [3]

questions.question: What baseline model is used?

result.answer:
The paper uses the same baseline as used by lang2011unsupervised, which assigns a semantic role to a constituent based on its syntactic function (the dependency relation to its head). [1]
A separate "supervised baseline" was constructed: for predicates seen in the supervised sentences, a MAP estimate of the parameters was calculated using the predefined mapping, while for unseen predicates the standard baseline was used. [2]

questions.question: What is the definition of offensive language?

result.answer:
该论文将帖子标记为冒犯性（OFF）的条件是：它包含任何形式的不可接受语言（亵渎）或带有目标的冒犯，后者可以是隐晦的或直接的。 [1]
该冒犯类别包括侮辱、威胁以及包含亵渎语言或脏话的帖子。 [1]
在 GermEval 共享任务中，冒犯类被细分为三类：亵渎、侮辱和虐待。 [2]
在 OLID 数据集中，作者使用分层标注模型，区分语言是否具有冒犯性，以及冒犯语言的类型和目标。 [3]

questions.question: Why masking words in the decoder is helpful?

desktop.error: 回答断言缺少当前正文支持或引用不一致

result.answer:
The refine decoder masks each word in the summary draft one by one, then feeds the draft to BERT to generate context vectors, and predicts the refined word given the other words of the summary. [1]
From the view of BERT or other contextualized embeddings, the refine decoding process provides a more complete input sequence consistent with their pre-training processes. [2]
Feeding bi-directional context instead of left-only context can better alleviate the problem of unnatural sequences caused by one-direction context. [3]

documents.title: Negated LAMA: Birds cannot fly

questions.question: How did they extend LAMA evaluation framework to focus on negation?

result.answer:
They created negated versions of Google-RE, T-REx and SQuAD by manually inserting a negation element in each template or statement. [1]
They did the same for a subset of ConceptNet that is easy to negate, selected by filtering for sentence length and extracting common queries. [1]
They state their approach differs from prior work by focusing on factual knowledge stored in negated statements. [2]
They contrast their work with BIBREF21, which used an entailment- and classification-based approach with fine-tuning, while they question to what extent factual knowledge in negated statements is indirectly acquired during pretraining. [3]
Their interpretation is that BERT mostly did not learn the meaning of negation, apparently ignoring negation markers in many cases. [4]
They note that negation had little effect on most queries and examined the small number of queries where models made correct predictions, giving examples such as “X did not die in Y” and “X was not born in Y”. [5]
尚待确认：The records do not explicitly state that the LAMA evaluation framework itself was extended; they describe creating negated versions of datasets (Google-RE, T-REx, SQuAD, ConceptNet subset).；The records do not describe the full evaluation methodology or metrics used for the negated datasets.

documents.title: Character-Level Question Answering with Attention

questions.question: What word level and character level model baselines are used?

result.answer:
The paper explores word-level models as an alternative to character-level models for constructing embeddings for questions, entities and predicates. [1]
The single character-level model achieves SQ accuracies of 70.9% and 70.3% on the FB2M and FB5M settings, respectively. [2]
The character-level model has 1.2M parameters, while the word-level model has 19.9M parameters. [2]
The word-level model achieves a best SQ accuracy of 53.9%. [2]
Both word-level and character-level models perform comparably well when predicting the predicate, reaching an accuracy of around 80%. [3]
The word-level model predicts only 45% of the entities accurately from the mixed set. [3]
The paper describes a character-level encoder-decoder framework that improves performance over state-of-the-art word-level neural models. [4]
Character-level modeling is presented as a way to handle the OOV issue, in contrast to word-level modeling. [5]

questions.question: What details are given about the Twitter dataset?

result.answer:
The Turkish Twitter corpus consists of tweets about Turkish mobile network operators and is described as mostly noisier and shorter than the movie corpus reviews. [1]
The Turkish Twitter corpus contains 1,716 tweets in total, of which 973 are negative and 743 are positive. [1]
The Turkish tweets were manually annotated by two humans with positive or negative labels, and the Cohen's Kappa inter-annotator agreement score was 0.82. [1]
Tweets with disagreement on polarity were removed from the Turkish Twitter corpus. [1]
A separate English Twitter dataset has nearly 1.6 million tweets annotated through a distant supervised method, with positive, neutral, and negative labels. [2]
From the English Twitter dataset, 7,020 positive tweets and 7,020 negative tweets were randomly selected to generate a balanced dataset. [2]
The reported accuracy for the English Twitter dataset was about 88 per cent. [3]
When the 3-feats technique is not taken into account, the corpus-based SVD method yields the highest accuracies for the English Twitter dataset. [4]
For the English Twitter dataset, accuracy decreases in some cases when polarity labels are utilised. [4]

第二个土耳其数据集是 Twitter 语料库，由关于土耳其移动网络运营商的推文组成。 [1]

另有一个英文 Twitter 数据集，含近 160 万条通过远程监督方法标注的推文，标签为正面、中性、负面；随机选取 7,020 条正面和 7,020 条负面推文构成平衡数据集。 [2]
在英文 Twitter 数据集上取得了约 88% 的准确率。 [3]
不考虑 3-feats 技术时，基于语料库的 SVD 方法在英文 Twitter 数据集上取得最高准确率。 [4]
对多数方法而言，电影语料库的成功率远高于 Twitter 数据集，因为推文通常更短、噪声更大。 [5]

From the Turkish movie corpus, 7,020 negative and 7,020 positive reviews were randomly selected and only those were processed. [1]
An English movie corpus collected from the web contains 5,331 positive reviews and 5,331 negative reviews. [2]
The English movie corpus was used to test the cross-linguality of the approaches. [2]
Accuracies of over 90 per cent were achieved for the Turkish movie corpus. [3]
The Turkish Twitter corpus tweets are described as mostly much noisier and shorter compared to the reviews in the movie corpus. [4]

questions.question: What approaches do they use towards text analysis?

result.answer:
The text describes supervised learning models for text analysis, with model choice guided by task definition and label types; for example, identifying stance towards rumors from sequential annotations could use an algorithm for learning from sequential or time-series data. [1]
Features used by models may range from content-based features such as single words, word sequences, or syntactic structure information, to meta-information such as user or network information. [1]
Selecting features requires experimentation and expert insight, often called feature engineering. [1]
For insight-driven analysis, human-interpretable features may be preferred because there is interest in why a prediction was made. [1]
Recent neural network approaches often use simple features as input, such as word embeddings or character sequences, requiring less feature engineering but making interpretation more difficult. [1]
The text frames computational text analysis as an addition to, not a replacement for, other approaches to analyzing social and cultural phenomena from textual data. [2]
The described approach moves back and forth between large-scale computational analyses and small-scale qualitative analyses to combine their strengths. [2]
Possible qualitative follow-ups mentioned include a qualitative discourse analyst examining a smaller corpus and an interview-methodology specialist reaching out to commenters. [2]
The text states that insight-driven computational analysis of text is becoming increasingly common and helps reveal broader views and subtle patterns. [3]
The text notes that cross-disciplinary work often involves discussion or negotiation about appropriate and feasible operationalization and analysis approaches. [3]
Local experts and “informants” can help navigate the data, including understanding an archive’s role and advising on data-collection strategies for underrepresented communities. [4]

questions.question: How was the spatial aspect of the EEG signal computed?

result.answer:
The spatial aspect was decoded from the channel covariance matrix using a CNN, specifically a four-layered 2D CNN stacking two convolutional and two fully connected hidden layers. [1]
At this first level of hierarchy, the CNN was trained with the corresponding labels as target outputs, optimizing a cross-entropy cost function. [1]
In parallel, a four-layered recurrent neural network (an LSTM with two fully connected hidden layers stacked with two LSTM layers) was applied to the channel covariance matrices to explore hidden temporal features. [1]
The last fully connected layer of the CNN was concatenated with its counterpart in the LSTM to form a single feature vector based on the two penultimate layers. [2]
This concatenation forms a joint spatio-temporal encoding of the cross-covariance matrix. [2]

questions.question: What is the goal of investigating NLP gender bias specifically in the news broadcast domain and Anchor role?

result.answer:
The paper frames gender bias in ASR as an open research question with no clear answer reached so far, and notes that many parameters must be taken into account to reach general agreement. [1]
The study's stated approach is to statistically describe gender representation in four French broadcast corpora, introducing the notion of speaker's role to refine the analysis in terms of voice professionalism. [1]
The study then questions the impact of that gender representation on an ASR system trained on these broadcast data. [1]
The paper cites prior work (BIBREF22) reporting better recognizer performance on female voice in a broadcast news and telephone corpus, with proposed explanations including more normative language and standard pronunciation for women linked to the traditional role of women in language acquisition and education. [2]
The paper reports that no significant gender bias was observed for prepared speech nor within the Anchor category, and that the median WER was smaller for women on prepared speech and equal to the male median WER for Anchor speakers. [3]
The paper states that the higher the degree of normativity of speech, the smaller the gender difference. [3]

questions.question: Do they inspect their model to see if their model learned to associate image parts with words related to entities?

result.answer:
The authors report that for the image-aided model (W+C+V), the modality attention attenuates irrelevant signals and amplifies relevant modality-based contexts when predicting a given token. [1]
The authors state that in training data, visual contexts are stronger indicators for named entities such as "space needle" and "splash mountain," and that the modality attention module attends more to stronger signals. [1]
In an error analysis, the authors describe cases where visual contexts affected named-entity prediction, e.g., visual tags helped disambiguate "curry" as a named entity and "Apple" as a non-named entity (a fruit). [2]

documents.title: Neural Architectures for Fine-Grained Propaganda Detection in News

questions.question: What extracted features were most influencial on performance?

result.answer:
For the FLC task, introducing polarity, POS and NER features into LSTM-CRF improved F1. [1]
For the FLC task, adding BERTSentEmb to multi-grained LSTM-CRF improved scores on dev (internal) but not on dev (external). [1]
For the SLC task, pre-trained embeddings (FastText or BERT) outperformed TF-IDF vector representation. [2]
For the SLC task, a logistic regression classifier with BERTSentEmb improved scores over FastTextSentEmb. [2]
For the SLC task, augmenting the sentence vector with additional features improved F1 on dev (external) but not on dev (internal). [2]
For the SLC task, initializing CNN with FastTextWordEmb or BERTWordEmb and augmenting the last hidden layer with BERTSentEmb and feature vectors led to F1 gains on both dev sets. [2]
The system used linguistic, layout and topical features across its neural architectures. [3]
The authors state they demonstrated gains in performance due to the features, ensemble schemes, multi-tasking and multi-granularity architectures. [3]
The linguistic features employed included sentiment, readability, emotion, part-of-speech and named entity tags, among others. [4]
尚待确认：The records do not provide a quantitative ranking of which extracted features were most influential overall.；The records do not report per-feature ablation results beyond the specific configurations described.

questions.question: What is specific to multi-granularity and multi-tasking neural arhiteture design?

result.answer:
The system reports performance gains attributable to multi-tasking and multi-granularity architectures, alongside features and ensemble schemes. [1]
For FLC, the authors designed a multi-task neural sequence tagger based on LSTM-CRF and linguistic features to jointly detect propagandistic fragments and their type. [2]
They investigated performing FLC and SLC jointly in a multi-granularity network based on LSTM-CRF and BERT. [2]
The multi-grain mode (LSTM-CRF+Multi-grain) jointly performs FLC and SLC using FastTextWordEmb and BERTSentEmb respectively, adding a binary sentence classification loss to sequence tagging weighted by a factor of α. [3]
The multi-task mode (LSTM-CRF+Multi-task) performs propagandistic span/fragment detection (PFD) and FLC (fragment detection + 19-way classification). [3]
Adding BERTSentEmb to the multi-grained LSTM-CRF improved scores on dev (internal) but not on dev (external). [4]
Multi-tasking was performed with another auxiliary task of PFD. [4]
Because it was difficult to infer the optimal configuration from dev scores, the two best configurations (II and IV) on dev (internal) were chosen and combined into an ensemble+ of predictions. [4]

questions.question: Does BERT reach the best performance among all the algorithms compared?

desktop.error: 回答断言缺少当前正文支持或引用不一致

result.answer:
在MEDDOCAN共享任务中，基于BERT的模型未能超过领域相关（S3）和领域无关（S2）NLNDE模型的得分。 [1]
BERT仅落后0.3个F1分数点，本可在MEDDOCAN共享任务所有参赛者中位列第二。 [1]
在训练数据稀缺实验中，基于BERT的模型表现出最高的鲁棒性，仅损失7个F1分数点。 [2]
尚待确认：记忆未明确说明在所有比较算法中BERT是否取得最佳整体性能（仅记录其在MEDDOCAN任务中未超过NLNDE模型、位列第二，以及在数据稀缺实验中鲁棒性最高）。

The datasets were transformed to comply with the BIO sequence representation scheme to feed the algorithms. [2]

questions.question: How is the vocabulary of word-like or phoneme-like units automatically discovered?

result.answer:
Raw acoustic feature-based unsupervised term discovery (UTD) aims to identify and cluster repeating word-like units across speech based around segmental dynamic time warping (DTW). [1]
A model-based alternative is unsupervised learning of hidden Markov model (HMM) based phoneme-like units from untranscribed speech. [1]
The acoustic unit discovery (AUD) framework used is nonparametric Bayesian, based on variational inference. [2]
In the AUD model, each phoneme-like unit is modeled as an HMM with a Gaussian mixture model of output densities (GMM-HMM) in a phone-loop model. [2]
Under the Dirichlet process framework, the phone loop is treated as an infinite mixture of GMM-HMMs, with mixture weights based on the stick-breaking construction. [2]
The infinite number of units in the mixture is truncated in practice, giving zero mixture weight to any unit beyond some large count. [2]
The mixture of GMM-HMMs is treated as a single unified HMM, and data segmentation is performed using the standard forward-backward algorithm. [2]
Training is fully unsupervised and parallelized; after a fixed number of training iterations, Viterbi decoding is used to obtain acoustic unit tokenizations of the data. [2]
AUD/ASR enables full-coverage segmentation of continuous speech into a sequence of units/words. [3]
UTD only identifies relatively long (0.5–1 sec) repeated terms. [3]

questions.question: What experiments are conducted?

result.answer:
The paper describes additional experiments on transforming ironic sentences into non-ironic sentences. [1]
The model was compared with other style transfer baselines using automatic and human evaluation results. [2]
During the experiments, the authors encountered the "No Change" issue, where style transfer models such as DualRL output the same input sentence. [3]
The authors addressed the "No Change" issue by tuning hyperparameters. [3]
During the experiments, the authors observed a word repetition issue in some outputs, as shown in Table TABREF38. [4]
To address word repetition, the authors lowered the decoding probability of a word if it had already been generated in previous time steps during testing. [4]
The authors also tried using a language model to control output fluency, but found pre-training a language model with tweets difficult due to casualness and noise. [4]

questions.question: What are the difficulties in modelling the ironic pattern?

result.answer:
The only high-quality irony dataset the authors could obtain was the Semeval-2018 Task 3 dataset, and it is pretty small, which will cause overfitting to complex models. [1]
Because of the small dataset, the authors implemented only a simple one-layer RNN with LSTM cell rather than a complex model. [1]
The authors observed that not all non-ironic sentences are suitable to be transferred into ironic sentences; for example, a sentence without an explicit sentiment polarity is hard to transfer. [1]
The sentiment analysis of ironic and non-ironic sentences differs, because in figurative language such as irony the sentiment polarity of the literal meaning may differ significantly from that of the intended figurative meaning. [2]
Because of this difference, using only one sentiment classifier was not enough, so the authors implemented two pre-trained sentiment classifiers, one for non-ironic and one for ironic sentences. [2]
The authors note that ironies in the latter two categories (other types of verbal irony and situational irony) are obscure and hard to understand, so they decided to focus only on the first category, verbal irony by means of a polarity contrast. [3]
The authors state there is a lack of previous work and baselines on irony generation, so they implemented their model based on style transfer. [3]
尚待确认：The records describe difficulties in irony detection/generation and dataset construction; they do not explicitly address difficulties in modelling an "ironic pattern" as such, so that specific framing cannot be confirmed.；No record states a formal list of modelling difficulties, responsible persons, or dates for resolving them.

documents.title: PitchNet: Unsupervised Singing Voice Conversion with Pitch Adversarial Network

questions.question: Are there elements, other than pitch, that can potentially result in out of key converted singing?

result.answer:
Singing voice conversion must handle a wider range of frequency variations and sharper changes of volume and pitch within singing voice than speech voice conversion. [1]
The performance of singing conversion is highly dependent on the musical expression of converted singing and the similarity of the converted voice timbre to the target singer's voice. [1]
The quality of generated singing often suffers due to the difficulty of learning a joint representation of phonetic and pitch representation. [1]
The input pitch can affect the output singing voice, as shown by qualitative analysis. [2]
PitchNet adds a pitch regression network to separate pitch information out of the latent space. [3]
In the dataset preparation, 8-bit mu-law encoding was used to reduce the input space and speed up training, although it degrades audio quality. [4]
尚待确认：The records do not explicitly state whether any factor other than pitch causes converted singing to be out of key.；The records do not provide a direct causal analysis linking volume changes, frequency variation, timbre similarity, or mu-law encoding to out-of-key output.

questions.question: How was annotation performed?

result.answer:
Annotation was performed using WebAnno, a web-based tool for linguistic annotation. [1]
Annotators could choose between a pre-annotated version or a blank version of each text. [1]
The pre-annotated versions contained suggested entity spans based on string matches from lists of conditions and findings synonym lists, and their quality varied widely throughout the corpus. [1]
The blank version was preferred by the annotators. [1]
The annotation was manual, covering all mentions of case entities, conditions, findings, factors and modifiers. [2]
The scope of manual annotation was limited to the presentation of a patient's signs and symptoms, and the title of the case report was also annotated. [2]
Discontinuous entities were modeled as a relation between two spans called "discontinuous". [3]
Nested entities were handled as fully-nested (one span completely embedded in another) or partially-nested (partial overlap between two entity spans). [3]

questions.question: What are improvements for these two approaches relative to ELMo-only baselines?

result.answer:
The paper investigates two methods: enhancing the ELMo architecture to allow pretraining on predicted shallow syntactic parses instead of just raw text, and classically adding chunk features to cwr-infused architectures for four downstream tasks. [1]
In both settings, the authors observe only modest gains on three of the four downstream tasks relative to ELMo-only baselines. [1]
Shallow syntactic features offer little to no benefit to ELMo models, and mSynC's performance is similar. [2]
On sentiment classification, chunk features are slightly harmful on average (with high variance), and mSynC again performs similarly to ELMo-transformer. [2]
The authors conclude that shallow syntax is not particularly helpful when using cwrs, as performance differences across all tasks are small. [2]
Overall, the findings indicate that ELMo-style pretraining discovers representations that make additional awareness of shallow syntax largely redundant. [3]

documents.title: Dice Loss for Data-imbalanced NLP Tasks

questions.question: How are weights dynamically adjusted?

result.answer:
该论文提出一种动态权重调整策略，为每个训练样本赋予与 (1-p) 成正比的权重。 [1]
该权重随训练进行而动态变化。 [1]
该策略在样本的 p 接近 1 时降低其权重，使模型关注难负样本，从而缓解易负样本的主导影响。 [1]
该策略受计算机视觉中 focal loss 的思想启发。 [1]
focal loss 通过加入 (1-p)^β 因子降低已良好分类样本的损失，最终损失为 (1-p)^β log p。 [2]
相关工作中，focal loss 采用软加权方案，在训练中强调较难的样本。 [3]
在自步学习中，样本权重通过优化加权训练损失获得，且每个训练步联合优化模型参数与样本权重。 [3]
其他工作根据训练损失调整不同训练样本的权重。 [3]
近期工作提出学习一个单独的网络来预测样本权重。 [3]
处理样本不等权重的两种常用策略是：为不同类别关联不同权重因子 α，或对数据集重采样。 [4]
